data.one_liner: SPKI SHA-256 TLS certificate pinning for Flutter with a drop-in HttpClient.
data.what_it_does: Provides a drop-in dart:io HttpClient implementation that enforces SPKI SHA-256 certificate pinning for secure connections. It also includes Ed25519 response signature checks on Flutter Web.
use_when: You need TLS certificate pinning to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on mobile and desktop.
You want a drop-in HttpClient replacement that works with package:http and package:dio.
avoid_when: You do not control your server keys and cannot ship backup pins before key rotations.
You are relying on native WebViews or plugins that use their own network stack without HttpOverrides.
strengths: Drop-in compatibility with dart:io HttpClient, package:http, and package:dio.
Supports per-host pin policies, wildcards, and unpinned host handling.
Includes cross-platform support including Android, iOS, desktop, and web signature checks.
weaknesses: Server key rotations without a backup pin will break the app until a client update is installed.
Flutter Web does not support TLS pinning and relies on a weaker response-signature scheme.
data.setup_notes: Requires obtaining your server certificate pins using OpenSSL or discovery mode and configuring minimum Android/iOS platform versions.
